Data:Stymphling.json.Desc: Eva Dewulf taught her father Valentine how to hatch these silvery little villains, but he never learnt to like them.

Data:Sugar.creamed.json.Label: Creamed Sugar
Data:Sugar.creamed.json.Desc: A precursor to Sticky Toffee Pudding (with bread) and to Fudge (without bread): both notorious as founding crimes of twentieth-century culinary debauchery.

Data:Sugar.json.Label: Sugar

Data:Suitcase.sb.json.Desc: A suitcase that once belonged to someone in the habit of shining a light in dark places.

Data:Sustenance.json.label: Sustenance
Data:Sustenance.json.desc: 'The bad live that they may eat and drink; the good eat and drink that they may live.' - Socrates

Data:Swaddled.thunder.json.Label: Swaddled Thunder
Data:Swaddled.thunder.json.Desc: A storm swathed in subtle threads, ready to be released with a few judicious snips.

xexts.scrutiny: The thread parts - the weave is empty - the skies cry out! [There are Keeper-level Heart recipes that can craft this from a Frith-Weft or a Thunderskin's Paean.]

Data:Sweetbones.numa.hint.json.label: Mist and Silence
Data:Sweetbones.numa.hint.json.startdescription: The door is open, the fire is cold, the shapes at the tables are hunched and quiet, dressed in furs and dark feathers. Mist presses against the walls and strokes the flagstones with its fingers. A drum taps an irregular rhythm somewhere beneath the inn. Numa.

Data:Symbol.solinvictis.json.Label: Sol Invictis Symbol
Data:Symbol.solinvictis.json.Desc: The eternal symbol of the Unconquered Sun, all the way back to the Shadowless Empire, even through the wild heresies of the Intercalate.

xexts.scrutiny: Since the Reformation, one quarter is assigned to each of the orthodox Hours - Madrugad, Watchman, Wolf, Meniscate - and the junction at the wheel's heart to the Sun in Rags or Splendour. A less orthodox tradition assigns the rim to the enigmatic St Januarius.

Data:Sympathy.carapace.json.label: Sympathy: Carapace
Data:Sympathy.carapace.json.desc: This one understands the possibilities of the Carapace Cross: alliance, awakening.

Data:Sympathy.chandler.json.label: Sympathy: Chandler
Data:Sympathy.chandler.json.desc: This one recognises the golden promise that the Chandler brings.

Data:Sympathy.reckoners.json.label: Sympathy: Reckoners
Data:Sympathy.reckoners.json.desc: This one understands the benefits of working with the merchants of years.

Data:Sympathy.ys.json.label: Sympathy: Ys
Data:Sympathy.ys.json.desc: This one understands the fragile benefits of an alliance with Ys.

Data:T.acatalogueofunchartedpleasures.js.Label: A Catalogue of Uncharted Pleasures
Data:T.acatalogueofunchartedpleasures.js.Desc: 'The Dark Gentleman' is the only, and rather grandiosely, identified author of this often-copied work.

xexts.reading．grail．intro: Some pleasures,' the Formulae Voluptuous attest, 'are so intense they can corrupt the laws of the physical world'. This text catalogues some of those instances.
xexts.reading．grail: Birth occurs at the conjunction of pleasure and torment. So the first Forbidden Acts of the Forge birthed sparks of delight which took root in the Glory or in Nowhere: who can say? So the seeds of the Flowermaker were planted, though for long years he was nothing but an unfulfilled ache.

Data:T.achildstreasuryofgoldenafternoons.Label: A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons
Data:T.achildstreasuryofgoldenafternoons.Desc: Once upon a time, a very bad man encoded very bad secrets into the charming illustrations of a book of charming stories. Wake the pictures, and you will see. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]

xexts.reading．edge．intro: Lord Jacob Gristwood: surgeon, ethnologist, philanthropist. There is no proof that he ever kept children in hutches beneath his bed. There is no proof he vivisected cats at dinner with his pen-knife. The Suppression Bureau keeps its secrets.
xexts.reading．edge: 'Here is your paint,' whispered the Wolf to the Pale Girl. 'Here is your knife-for-scraping. And here is your face.'

Data:T.adescentoftheshell.json.Label: A Descent of the Shell
Data:T.adescentoftheshell.json.Desc: A treatise on eggs, light, and optics by Abbess Melancthe, dazzlingly illuminated with renderings of the Abbess' visions.

xexts.reading．forge．intro: The book is unexpectedly challenging to read. The bright glitter of the gold-leaf illuminations acquires a migrainous quality; the eye aches and tires…
xexts.reading．forge: This is, most likely, the 'certain vivid book' that Melancthe once sent to Gunnhild, daughter of King Harold, which provoked in her 'a dream of eyes' but also caused her to begin to lose her sight (until she was healed by the saint-bishop Wulfstan). To complete it is a kind of test. Its double thesis, at last, seems to be that the Sun is either an eye or an egg; and so the Second Dawn will be either its opening, or its hatching.

Data:T.adviceoncontainment.json.Label: Advice on Containment
Data:T.adviceoncontainment.json.Desc: Thirza Blake discusses ways 'to keep Wood-things out of trouble, and Mansus-things in it.'

xexts.reading．knock．intro: Thirza is irritatingly light on specifics, insisting above all that the duties of an adept are the duties of a host, and that a conjured spirit should be kept in as luxurious a vessel as possible.
xexts.reading．knock: Thirza notes the similarities between the Lantern-long habit of 'scrining' - returning to the physical world, despite their absence of a body, by entering a mirror or light - and Poemander's techniques of confining Mansus-long to mirrors. She wonders whether Poemander himself might be lured to visit Hush House if provided with a sufficiently alluring scrine.

Data:T.againstthesisterhoodoftheknotandt.Label: Against the Sisterhood of the Knot and the Foulness of their Depraved Customs
Data:T.againstthesisterhoodoftheknotandt.Desc: Hieronymus Pseudo-Hypnerotomachus wrote this furious screed about the sinister influence of the Sisterhood of the Knot on his own Church of the Unconquered Sun.

xexts.reading．sky．intro: Hieronymus claims that the powers served by the Sisterhood of the Knot made an arrangement: the Thunderskin loved the Yew, and the Grail destroyed him, as restitution for the destruction of the Axe's loved ones. Hieronymus' writing becomes incoherent with rage at this point.
xexts.reading．sky: Hieronymus recovers his composure, eventually, to describe how the Thunderskin entered the Mansus through the Peacock Door. This, Hieronymus insists, is 'abomination upon abomination: but then that most abominable of Doors has always been an abomination.'

Data:T.againstvitruvius.json.Label: Against Vitruvius
Data:T.againstvitruvius.json.Desc: A fourteenth-century treatise on esoteric mechanics and parahydraulics by Abbot Ranulph, best known now as a mason-architect.

xexts.reading．sky．intro: Ranulph describes how he tested some of these techniques in the construction of the Winter Tower (now called the Long Tower). He admits to unexpected consequences…
xexts.reading．sky: Ranulph mentions that the tower of Ely Cathedral collapsed around the time the Winter Tower was completed… although he stops short of suggesting that one was the cause of another. 'A tower falls, a tower rises,' is all he'll commit to.

Data:T.ajourneytothegrove.json.Label: A Journey to the Grove
Data:T.ajourneytothegrove.json.Desc: Black Elie, who much later became Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Knot, recounts her journey to the Grove of Green Immortals.

xexts.reading．grail．intro: In the Grove, Elie meets with an entity identified as 'Three Faces, Nine Colours' - who may have become her lover.
xexts.reading．grail: Three Faces is a Name of the Applebright, the Nowhere Hour of youth, healing and mutation. It offers Elie a form of eternal youth to take back West with her, which she rejects for certain reasons. She does promise, however, to renew their acquaintance 'in the season when the Applebright is the Witch' - not from sentiment, but rather grandly, to ensure the continuity of the Histories.

Data:T.alightintheinkwell.json.Label: A Light in the Inkwell
Data:T.alightintheinkwell.json.Desc: Musgrave, fourth of the Dewulf line, writes tentatively about the 'Covenant of Brancrug' and the legacy of the sacred inks he calls 'encausta revelationia'.

xexts.reading．lantern．intro: 'Words are of the First Importance. So the Book of Suns teaches. But do not Words require Ink? And is the Inkwell not then the Womb of Words?'
xexts.reading．lantern: Musgrave identifies 'the Ichor Auroral' as the mother of the encaustum Porphyrine. He adds that it would be blasphemous to describe the origins of the Ichor itself, although a scrawled marginal note suggests a later reader thought Musgrave was only hiding his ignorance beneath a cloak of piety.

Data:T.amanualfordeparture.json.Label: A Manual for Departure
Data:T.amanualfordeparture.json.Desc: The author, who identifies itself as the Jekadu, claims to be one of the Great Hooded Princes of the Land of the River. The style is informal, even chatty.

xexts.reading．knock．intro: 'No, these doors shouldn't be recorded, but if we had only recorded things before we'd had to leave the Fifth History, we would be in a much better state. So here I am writing it down, and if you don't like it you can sanction me.'
xexts.reading．knock: The 'Manual for Departure' lists a number of strategies - occult, martial and political - for quick escapes. Many are irrelevant, obsolete or enigmatic, but the Manual does include a number of powerful techniques for opening portals.

Data:T.ambrosial!.json.Label: Ambrosial!
Data:T.ambrosial!.json.Desc: Ambrose Westcott's inventive - one might say pioneering, or indeed buccaneering - essays into kitchencraft.

xexts.reading．forge．intro: Westcott proudly announces his intention to transform cuisine to become 'an Engine of Alchemy, a Fount of War.'
xexts.reading．forge: Westcott compares the ferocity of fire with the intensity of appetite as 'in essence, one essence'. A fire's ability to transform and destroy grows when it is offered the correct fuel; so too, he implies, can a sufficiently inspired appetite allow its possessor to consume 'greatly, strangely, unwisely.'

Data:T.amiranisbeteli.json.Label: Amiranis Beteli
Data:T.amiranisbeteli.json.Desc: A fragment of iron-alloy meteorite carefully inscribed and polished. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]

xexts.reading．forge．intro: 'Who gave us fire? Who gave us steel? What is the sound of dusk? Of what alloy is wind forged?'
xexts.reading．forge: Esoteric secrets of metallurgy and resonance are revealed - including directions towards the creation of a terrible Bell.

Data:T.analmanacofentrances.json.Label: An Almanac of Entrances
Data:T.analmanacofentrances.json.Desc: A handbook of sealed and unsealed byways and shortcuts through the Bounds, compiled by Willem Harries in the 1860s - during his term as Librarian of Hush House.

xexts.reading．knock．intro: Harries discusses the role played by the 'Légion du Seuil' and the 'Company of the Wolf-in-Gold' in warding the Bounds against outside influences. He warns that Bounds-travellers may themselves be considered 'outside influences…'
xexts.reading．knock: 'The Mansus, as Ys, lacks walls; Ys and the Mansus have both their gates, and there may be no gate without a wall. Thus the paradox resolves, as all those who walk in dream will learn. But the Wood has neither gate nor wall, and so it is the Wood whose roots may creep after us into the hours of our waking.'

Data:T.anechoofsilence.json.Label: An Echo of Silence
Data:T.anechoofsilence.json.Desc: A very heterodox history of the House of Lethe as recorded by 'the Serenity' - a Lethean adept who declares that the House of Lethe was created explicitly to prevent the ascension of any more mortals to Name or Hour status.

xexts.reading．moth．intro: 'Eternity cannot be escaped; but in History, it may be delayed,' the Serenity explains. 'The gods-who-were-flesh, by their nature, are a surrender to Eternity.'
xexts.reading．moth: The 'roots of the House' are said to pass into the Wood of dreams through three forests in the Bounds, identified as the Bei Ilai, the Black Cedar Forest, and the Brecheliant. 'While one tree of these may yet stand, one single tree, the Histories continue.'

Data:T.anexorcistsfieldmanual.json.Label: An Exorcist's Field Manual
Data:T.anexorcistsfieldmanual.json.Desc: A practical guide to 'troublesome Dead', grounded in theory but with a clear focus on their disposal, by the redoubtable Detective-Ostiary Wheelock of the Suppression Bureau.

xexts.reading．moon．intro: 'The Dead usually avoid Light - as the most immediate manifestation of Eternity, which has no place for death. However those Dead 'uplifted by gold', that is to say touched by an actinic theoplasma, happily bod about in daylight and are perhaps strongest at noon...'
xexts.reading．moon: 'If you are dead but 'uplifted by green', that's the Ring-Yew's blessing. (The Crowned Growth offers a similar but nastier benefit.) This is how Burgeoning Risen come about, but there are different degrees of sentience and freedom depending on which growths are involved. The consciousness of one 'uplifted by green' is always greatly altered, though - they never really seem like the same person. They may have dregs of their original souls, but these are often replaced by something else. The upshot, invariably, is that they need to be set firmly on fire.'

Data:T.animpertinentvitulation.json.Label: An Impertinent Vitulation
Data:T.animpertinentvitulation.json.Desc: A book of kitchen-garden techniques and aphrodisiac recipes recorded by Ernestine Peterhans, the 'Iron Seneschale' of Hush House for three generations of Dewulfs.

xexts.reading．grail．intro: Peterhans asserts casually that the rousing liquor called 'Rubywise Ruin', which Leaves & Thorns techniques can brew from flowers, was a favourite of the notoriously severe Baron Thomas. If true, this would have raised eyebrows had it been known in his lifetime...
xexts.reading．grail: Peterhans mentions that one of these Leaves & Thorns techniques, with sufficient Nectar aspect, can supposedly cause 'a marvellous copper fruit' to burst from wood, although she has never managed it herself - but in a 'certain season' the pear-trees in the Practic Garden will deliver something similar.
